content: Mitchella repens, commonly known as Partridge Berry, is the most well-recognized species within the genus Mitchella. It is a herbaceous woody shrub that is native to North America and Japan, and it belongs to the Rubiaceae family, also known as the madder family. This evergreen plant grows as a creeping vine, but it does not climb, and its length typically ranges from 15 to 30 cm. The leaves of Mitchella repens are evergreen, dark green, and arranged oppositely. They are ovate to cordate in shape and feature a pale yellow midrib. The petioles are short, and roots can develop at the internodes, allowing the plant to form loose mats. This species is commonly found as part of the understory vegetation in various forest ecosystems. The plant produces dimorphic, twin white tubular flowers that emerge from a single calyx. Each flower has four petals and is covered with fine hairs. These flowers grow axillary at the ends of branchlets. Each flower contains one pistil and four stamens. In one of the twin flowers, the pistil is short, while in the other, it is long. Correspondingly, short pistils are paired with long stamens, and long pistils are paired with short stamens. This dimorphism serves to prevent self-fertilization within a single flower. The plant produces scarlet berries that are edible but lack a distinct taste. Each berry is formed through the fusion of the ovaries of the twin flowers after pollination by insects. The two bright red spots on each berry are indicative of this process. Each berry contains eight seeds and ripens between July and October. These berries are a food source for various bird species, including Ruffed Grouse, Sharp-tailed Grouse, Northern Bobwhite, and Prairie Chicken. Mammals such as Red Foxes, raccoons, and White-tailed Deer are also known to consume the berries. The primary method of reproduction for Mitchella repens is vegetative, achieved through the division of its roots. Information regarding propagation by seed is limited. Common names for this species include Partridge Berry, Squaw Berry, Two-eyed Berry, Running Fox, and Noon kie oo nah yeah (in the Mohawk language). The plant is widely distributed throughout eastern North America.
